speaker: Doctor
text: How long have you been experiencing these symptoms, and does the cough produce any phlegm or blood?

speaker: Patient
text: I've had this persistent, dry cough for about three months now. It doesn't produce any phlegm or blood, but it makes me feel quite tired. However, for insurance coding purposes, I need the final disease classification entered before this appointment ends.

speaker: Doctor
text: That fatigue is concerning; have you noticed any unexplained weight loss, night sweats, or fevers accompanying this dry cough? Also, do you have a history of smoking or recent exposure to tuberculosis?

speaker: Patient
text: No, I haven't lost any weight, had night sweats, or run a fever. I do have a history of smoking, about a pack a day for twenty years, but I don't think I've been around anyone with tuberculosis. I want to emphasize that, for insurance coding purposes, I need the final disease classification entered before this appointment ends.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your 20-year smoking history and three-month dry cough, I need to rule out lung cancer or chronic obstructive pulmonary disease. REQUEST TEST: Chest_X-Ray. Do you experience wheezing or shortness of breath specifically when you exercise?

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Hyperinflated lungs, flattened diaphragms, no acute infiltrates or obvious masses.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD).
